findings: All four requested font declarations yield the same mixed and Han-separated widths at six displayed decimals. Adjacent punctuation differs by only 0.000015 CSS px between groups.
This sample does not support fixing punctuation width merely by removing explicit fallback families, switching the system generic, or setting font-kerning:normal.
Computed font-family identifies the requested CSS declaration, not the actual font for each shaped glyph. Equal widths do not prove font identity.
All groups repeat at 17.218750 CSS px under requested 17.22px; this is local Range/element geometry, not Apple Notes baseline evidence.
The AX capture has complete summary table values but only a truncated textarea JSON prefix. No complete per-character JSON export exists in this evidence.
limitations: Safari result does not prove the bundled app WKWebView uses identical engine configuration or font fallback.
DOM Range advance/rects, CoreText native points, PDF export coordinates and screenshot ink bounds are distinct measurements.
The visible devicePixelRatio=2 belongs to this Safari page only; it does not establish the DPR of previously captured app images.
text-spacing-trim and chws/palt values were not probed by this page. Their current local CSS parsing, computed values and actual shaping effects remain unmeasured.
CSS.supports for a generic font-feature-settings declaration cannot establish that a specific font implements a tag or that shaping applied it.

measurements: Keep the three frozen strings, isolated punctuation and ordinary Han/Latin controls; record compact complete JSON of whole-line widths and prefix differences.
Keep font size, line height, kerning, text-rendering, language and available width fixed. Do not combine trimming and manual font-feature controls in the first pass.

If a control changes only adjacent punctuation while leaving Han-separated and plain text stable, it distinguishes a contextual adjustment candidate; if isolated/nonadjacent widths also change, retain those regressions explicitly.
Only after one discriminating control is found, capture the winning single candidate and baseline in the actual app; do not modify production CSS based on Safari alone.
